title: Unique Paths II
statement_short: Given an m x n integer array obstacleGrid, return the number of possible unique paths from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner. Movement is restricted to down or right, and obstacles marked as 1 cannot be traversed.
constraints: m == obstacleGrid.length, n == obstacleGrid[i].length, 1 <= m, n <= 100, obstacleGrid[i][j] is 0 or 1
hint: Grid bounds up to 100x100 permit 2D DP path accumulation, setting blocked obstacle cells to 0 ways.
keywords: obstacles marked as 1 cannot be traversed
why_not: Right: 2D DP accumulates path counts from top and left neighbors, setting obstacle cells to 0 in O(m \* n) time and O(n) space. Not Graph BFS: Queue-based grid traversal counts path ways, but 2D DP handles state tabulation without queue management memory. Not Backtracking: Recursive path exploration without state memoization causes TLE in O(2^(m+n)) time. Not Math / Geometry: Combinatorial formula C(m+n-2, m-1) calculates obstacle-free paths, but fails when arbitrary obstacle grids block paths.
